exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `legacy_id` is an auto-generated row id, referenced by intakes.csv and consents.jsonl
exportNotesClaims.note: 0 duplicate id values; 21 intake rows and 0 consent events reference an id that is not in patients.csv.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `full_name` is as typed by the patient or ops
exportNotesClaims.note: The export carries no provenance per field. The inventory shows the variation that "as typed" implies.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `email` is the primary contact and was also used as a login by one automation
exportNotesClaims.note: Login use is not visible in the export. 44 case-insensitive duplicate groups and 16 values failing the syntax check mean the column is not a unique identifier as exported.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `dob` is the date of birth
exportNotesClaims.note: 921 values read as two different calendar dates depending on the ordering, 0 shapes carry both an unambiguous day-first and an unambiguous month-first value, and the shapes point in opposite directions: `9999-99-99` month-first only (1118 of 1828), `99-99-9999` day-first only (207 of 328), `99/99/9999` month-first only (154 of 310). 5 values read as a date after 2026-09-08 under every ordering.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `sex` is whatever the form or the ops person entered at the time
exportNotesClaims.note: 11 raw spellings, 7 after folding, Dutch and English mixed.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `bsn` is a Dutch citizen service number, never validated
exportNotesClaims.note: 17 of 941 nine-digit values fail the elfproef.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `phone` format was never enforced
exportNotesClaims.note: 4 distinct shapes.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `city` is self-reported
exportNotesClaims.note: Provenance is not in the export; 0 folded values have more than one raw spelling.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `weight` / `weight_unit` is weight at signup, with the unit column added late and backfilled "where obvious"
exportNotesClaims.note: 18 rows have no unit and 55 say lbs; 45 rows sit outside a 15..70 BMI window under the kilogram reading but inside it under the pound reading. When the backfill happened is not visible.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `height_cm` was always intended as centimetres
exportNotesClaims.note: 0 values below 3, 4 in 3..100, 0 in 100..140 and 1 at 220 or more.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `status` is roughly active / paused / churned / prospect, spelled many ways
exportNotesClaims.note: 17 raw spellings, 11 after folding, including Dutch words and trailing whitespace.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `signup_date` is when the row was created
exportNotesClaims.note: 3 rows are dated after the reference date 2026-09-08 under every plausible ordering.

exportNotesClaims.claim: patients.csv: `source` is the funnel: `typeform`, `website`, campaign tags, `import`
exportNotesClaims.note: Values present but not named in the notes: `referral`.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `intake_id` is the form tool submission id
exportNotesClaims.note: 0 id values appear on more than one row.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `legacy_patient_id` should reference patients.csv:legacy_id, but the automation occasionally fired before the patient row existed
exportNotesClaims.note: 21 rows do not resolve; 297 resolvable intakes are dated before their patient's signup_date under at least one ordering and 0 under every ordering.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `submitted_at` is the submission date
exportNotesClaims.note: The column carries several shapes and 1033 values that read as two different dates.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `questionnaire_version` labelling discipline varied
exportNotesClaims.note: 5 distinct raw values including an empty one.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `weight` / `height` are self-reported at submission time and can legitimately differ from patients.csv
exportNotesClaims.note: They do differ, and 26 rows differ by roughly the kilogram/pound factor, which is not a difference "self-reported" explains on its own.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `meds_current` is free text, never normalised
exportNotesClaims.note: 30 distinct folded values; 9 rows list several medications separated by a comma and 5 folded values match the empty-like heuristic.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `conditions` is free text, Dutch and English mixed
exportNotesClaims.note: Each row in one class: 1814 rows carry a Dutch-only spelling, 0 an English-only condition name, 185 the English placeholder `none`, 731 a spelling that is the same in both languages (`diabetes type 2`, `pancreatitis 2022`, `pcos`, `prediabetes`, `reflux`) and 187 are empty.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `alcohol_units_week` is self-reported units per week
exportNotesClaims.note: 1 distinct non-empty value is not a number, on 272 rows.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `outcome` is approved / rejected / pending, spelled many ways, and is distinct from the patient-level status
exportNotesClaims.note: 10 distinct folded values plus 0 empty ones; 0 folded values appear in both this column and patients.csv.status.

exportNotesClaims.claim: intakes.csv: `reviewer_note` is a free-text note by the reviewing doctor, if any
exportNotesClaims.note: Only 5 distinct values appear, so the column behaves as a small template set rather than free text, and it carries no reviewer identity.

exportNotesClaims.claim: consents.jsonl: `patient_legacy_id` references patients.csv:legacy_id
exportNotesClaims.note: 0 events do not resolve; 99 patients have no event.

exportNotesClaims.claim: consents.jsonl: `type` has only `data_processing` in this export
exportNotesClaims.note: Values present: `data_processing`.

exportNotesClaims.claim: consents.jsonl: `action` is `granted` or `revoked`
exportNotesClaims.note: Values present: `granted`, `revoked`.

exportNotesClaims.claim: consents.jsonl: `at` is the widget-side event timestamp
exportNotesClaims.note: 0 of the timestamps carry a timezone suffix, so the offset behind "widget-side" is not recorded.

exportNotesClaims.claim: consents.jsonl: `version` is the consent-text version the patient saw
exportNotesClaims.note: Values present: `v2`, `v1`; the export contains no consent texts to compare against.

exportNotesClaims.claim: Caveat: several automations plus manual ops edits wrote to patients.csv over the years
exportNotesClaims.note: No provenance column exists, but format and vocabulary differ measurably by source and by year.

exportNotesClaims.claim: Caveat: consents.jsonl is one JSON object per line, append-only
exportNotesClaims.note: 0 lines fail to parse as a JSON object; 131 patients have a file order that differs from their timestamp order, which an append-only log would not produce on its own.

exportNotesClaims.claim: Caveat: consents are believed complete from 2023 onwards; before that nobody is sure
exportNotesClaims.note: 477 events are dated before 2023-01-01, and 432 patients have no event dated 2023 or later. Completeness cannot be checked from inside the export.

exportNotesClaims.claim: Caveat: the form tool was set to ISO at some point in 2024; before that it depended on the automation, at least one of them US-style
exportNotesClaims.note: 111 intakes dated 2024 or later still carry a non-ISO shape (and 403 intakes before 2024 are already ISO); for signup_date the figures are 128 and 564. Non-ISO shapes appear in every year.

exportNotesClaims.claim: Caveat: weights are probably kilograms, an early expat campaign briefly offered pounds, and the unit column was backfilled "where obvious"
exportNotesClaims.note: 55 rows carry `lbs` and 18 carry no unit; 45 rows read plausibly only as pounds, and 26 intake/patient weight ratios sit near the 2.20462 factor.

exportNotesClaims.claim: Caveat: status values were typed by different automations and different humans over time
exportNotesClaims.note: 17 raw spellings, and the vocabulary differs by source and by year.

exportNotesClaims.claim: Caveat: BSNs were collected for a period, then the field was hidden from the form, and were never validated
exportNotesClaims.note: Non-empty bsn values appear in signup years 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2062 out of 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025, 2026, 2062, so the collection window is not visible as a clean cut; 17 of 941 nine-digit values fail the elfproef.

exportNotesClaims.claim: Caveat (ops): "some people definitely signed up twice with different emails to retry the intake"
exportNotesClaims.note: 31 name-plus-dob groups exist, 3 of them span more than one folded email.

notWarnedAbout.finding: 44 email addresses appear on more than one row once case is folded, and 547 local-parts appear on more than one domain.
103 rows give an age at signup below 18 and 1 above 100.
3 signup dates and 3 intake dates lie after the reference date 2026-09-08 under every plausible ordering.
30 bsn values are shared by more than one row, which is an identity collision rather than a formatting problem.
61 phone numbers are shared by more than one row when compared on digits only.
72 full_name values carry leading or trailing whitespace, which splits 20 name groups that folding would join; 0 names contain a digit and 0 are ALL CAPS.
The reviewer_note "twijfel, toch akkoord" (doubt, agreed anyway) appears on 421 intakes, of which 73 have a rejecting outcome and 49 an outcome that is neither an approval nor a rejection.
5 patients submitted more than one intake on the same day (dates compared on any shared plausible reading) and 0 row groups are identical in every field except intake_id.
7 patients have a revoke with no prior grant in the log.
131 patients get a different derived consent state depending on whether the log is read in timestamp order or in file order, and 131 patients have events written out of timestamp order.
99 patients have no consent event at all, which is not the same as a revoked consent.
69 consent events are dated after the reference date 2026-09-08.
alcohol_units_week mixes numbers with 1 non-numeric spelling on 272 rows, next to 290 empty values, so "no alcohol" and "not answered" are not distinguishable by type alone.

21 intake rows reference a patient id that patients.csv does not contain (21 distinct ids, of which 0 also appear in consents.jsonl), and the notes mention only that the automation could fire early, not that the rows would stay unresolved in the export.
14 rows carry a date that sits after a gap of more than a year from every other date in its column, so the latest dates in the export are outliers rather than a boundary.
5 dob values read as a date after the reference date 2026-09-08 under some ordering, 5 under every ordering.
Whether an intake predates its patient row is itself undecided: 297 intakes are earlier than signup_date under at least one date ordering, while 0 are earlier under every ordering.
26 intake weights are between 0.4 and 0.5 times the patient-row weight and 31 are below 0.4 times it, so the disagreement between the two columns is not only the self-reporting the notes describe.
The 18 rows with no weight_unit all carry a weight, and their median sits far from the median of the kg rows, so "backfilled where obvious" left a group that reads as neither.
5 patient weights are below 35 and 9 are 300 or more, neither of which the kg-or-lbs story explains.
30 email values carry leading or trailing whitespace, 10 carry whitespace inside the address and 28 contain uppercase, so the column the notes call a login is not comparable as exported.
410 intakes carry no questionnaire_version, so the ruleset that evaluated them is not recorded.
251 status values and 385 outcome values carry trailing whitespace, so a plain string comparison splits states that read identically.
